campaign_note: After Apple's 2026-08-06 patch, NCSC-NL reported abuse on multiple internet-exposed Macs (TCP/5900) resulting in root access and a Monero miner, and Microsoft reported exploitation on a limited number of devices; no compromise count is published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: NCSC-NL advisory update, as reported by BleepingComputer (the NCSC-NL update's own date was not shown; Apple's advisory carries no exploitation statement)

evidence.counts_what: Internet-reachable hosts with Screen Sharing open (exposed product, not confirmed vulnerable); single researcher scan
evidence.measured_by: Independent researcher @osxreverser, quoted by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: My last scan shown around 40k open screen sharing hosts on the internet, almost half in the U.S.

evidence.counts_what: Macs with port 5900 internet-exposed on which abuse was observed, with root access and a Monero miner installed (qualitative)
evidence.measured_by: NCSC-NL (from a notification it received), quoted by BleepingComputer
evidence.quote: has received a notification indicating that active abuse of this vulnerability has been observed on multiple systems

evidence.value: limited number of macOS devices; no count
evidence.counts_what: Devices on which Microsoft observed active exploitation (qualitative)
evidence.measured_by: Microsoft (X post), quoted by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: limited number of macOS devices

campaign_note: Apple patched this CoreGraphics zero-day on 2026-09-28, crediting Meta Product Security and stating it may have been exploited against specific targeted individuals; no delivery vector, actor or victim count is public.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Apple security advisory (CoreGraphics entry, credited to Meta Product Security)

evidence.counts_what: Vendor statement of exploitation scope (qualitative, no number)
evidence.quote: Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27.

campaign_note: On 2026-03-19 an actor tracked as TeamPCP used compromised credentials to publish a malicious Trivy v0.69.4 and force-push credential-stealing code to trivy-action and setup-trivy tags, with follow-on compromises of Checkmarx KICS and LiteLLM; Mandiant's victim count is for the threat actor's campaign as a whole, not Trivy alone.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Aqua Security / public reporting of the compromise on the day it occurred, per Microsoft Security blog (2026-03-24); Aqua's advisory GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23 was published 2026-03-21

evidence.counts_what: Impacted SaaS environments dealing with this threat actor (lower bound, 'over 1,000'; campaign-wide TeamPCP figure following the Trivy compromise, not Trivy-only); spoken statement at a Google event at RSA Conference
evidence.measured_by: Mandiant Consulting (Charles Carmakal, CTO), reported by The Register
evidence.quote: We know of over 1,000 impacted SaaS environments right now that are actively dealing with this particular threat actor

evidence.counts_what: GitHub workflow files referencing aquasecurity/trivy-action (lower bound, 'over 10,000'; exposed users of the product, not confirmed to have run the malicious tags)
evidence.measured_by: Socket (Philipp Burckhardt), quoted by The Register
evidence.quote: With over 10,000 workflow files on GitHub referencing this action, the potential blast radius is significant

evidence.counts_what: Version tags in aquasecurity/trivy-action force-pushed to credential-stealing commits (plus all 7 setup-trivy tags)
evidence.quote: The attacker force-pushed 76 of 77 version tags to malicious commits that injected an infostealer into `entrypoint.sh`.

evidence.counts_what: Exposure window during which malicious trivy-action tags were live (2026-03-19 ~17:43 UTC to 2026-03-20 ~05:40 UTC); other components ~3, ~4 and ~10 hours. A malicious-distribution window, not service downtime
Aqua Security internal GitHub repositories renamed/defaced and exposed by the attackers
evidence.measured_by: Paul McCarty (researcher), reported by The Register
evidence.quote: renaming all 44 repositories and exposing internal source code, CI/CD configs, and knowledge bases

campaign_note: Atlassian published the advisory on 2026-10-05, watchTowr published technical details and a PoC on 2026-10-06, and Previdian honeypots saw exploitation attempts within two hours; watchTowr reported fingerprinting and config-file sweeps with no post-compromise activity observed.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Previdian honeypot telemetry (Help Net Security says attempts began 'late Tuesday', i.e. 2026-10-06; BleepingComputer's 2026-10-07 article says 'earlier today')

evidence.counts_what: Exploitation attempts against Previdian's honeypot network, from three unique IP addresses; measurement window not stated; not a compromise count
evidence.measured_by: Previdian, reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: a total of 15 exploitation attempts have been detected from three unique IP addresses located in Japan and the U.S.

evidence.counts_what: Attacking IP addresses seen by Previdian honeypots (38.60.157.86, 146.70.187.234, 159.26.119.225)
evidence.quote: observed attempts from these three IP addresses: 38.60.157[.]86, 146.70.187[.]234, and 159.26.119[.]225

evidence.counts_what: Character of observed exploitation (qualitative)
evidence.quote: Most attempts at exploitation so far have focused on fingerprinting the existence of an affected product

campaign_note: mySites.guru found the Balbooa Forms (Joomla) upload flaw being exploited as a zero-day on 2026-07-08 via a customer's hosting abuse report; Balbooa shipped 2.4.1 on 2026-07-09 and no count of compromised sites has been published.

evidence.value: 1 customer site (single self-report); no wider count
evidence.counts_what: Live attack on one mySites.guru customer that led to discovery (qualitative)
evidence.measured_by: mySites.guru, reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: The vulnerability was discovered by mySites.guru on July 8, 2026, following a live attack on one of its customers.
